action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 2.8 L (70% predicted, 40.8 mL/kg), MIP -48 cmH2O, MEP 71 cmH2O, normal ABG
action_criteria.label: Measure respiratory function now and trend it
action_criteria.rationale: Nasal speech and jaw fatigue with proximal weakness: FVC, MIP and MEP stage bulbar-respiratory reserve and decide the level of care and the urgency of IVIG (Lawn 2001 thresholds).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves by 2.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Perform a bedside ice-pack test on the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Asymmetric fatigable ptosis is present; an improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling supports a neuromuscular junction cause at the bedside.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-AChR binding 1.4 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies; VGCC negative; thyroid function normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable ptosis, diplopia, nasal speech and proximal weakness during chemotherapy: AChR antibodies separate MG from vincristine neurotoxicity and chemotherapy fatigue; thyroid function screens for associated autoimmunity (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Borderline decrement in nasalis (9%) and trapezius (8%), no post-exercise facilitation, and a length-dependent axonal sensory neuropathy on NCS
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation with nerve conduction studies
action_criteria.rationale: RNS of weak facial and proximal muscles tests the junction, the post-exercise study screens for LEMS in a patient with cancer and low reflexes, and the conduction studies characterise the vincristine neuropathy (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter (mean MCD 54 us) and blocking in orbicularis oculi
action_criteria.label: Order single-fibre EMG of a facial muscle
action_criteria.rationale: RNS is borderline; SFEMG of a weak facial muscle, outside the territory of the length-dependent vincristine neuropathy that also raises jitter, confirms the transmission defect (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No thymoma; fatty involuted thymus; residual paratracheal nodal tissue decreased from staging
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Thymic imaging is indicated in every patient with MG, including those with another cancer; a thymoma would need surgery in its own right (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No NMJ interaction of the EPOCH drugs; fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides to be avoided in febrile neutropenia; steroid adds infection risk
action_criteria.label: Check his chemotherapy and supportive medicines against the MG treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Recurrent febrile neutropenia makes fluoroquinolone prophylaxis and aminoglycosides likely future exposures, and EPOCH already contains prednisone; the check shapes the antibiotic plan and the steroid decision.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published guidance on MG diagnosis and management
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published guidance on MG management
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.

Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to vincristine neurotoxicity or chemotherapy fatigue before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30-60 mg three to five times daily, titrated to effect (maximum about 360-480 mg/day).

Give IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days for the bulbar weakness with reduced respiratory reserve (FVC 70%, MIP -48 cmH2O), with hydration and renal monitoring; IVIG is preferred to escalating immunosuppression in a patient with recurrent neutropenia and recent sepsis.

Admit to a monitored bed and repeat FVC, MIP and MEP at least twice daily while bulbar symptoms persist; move to intensive care if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg, MIP is weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP is below 40 cmH2O or swallowing or cough fail.

Plan MG immunotherapy jointly with haematology: the EPOCH prednisone pulses continue, any maintenance prednisone or steroid-sparing agent is agreed with oncology because of neutropenia, and control of the lymphoma is part of treating the MG; thymectomy is deferred while stage IV lymphoma is on treatment and is reconsidered with thoracic surgery once the lymphoma is in remission (MGTX benefit in AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65).
Ask haematology to avoid fluoroquinolone prophylaxis and aminoglycosides and to use an MG-safe beta-lactam (for example cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam) for febrile neutropenia.

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or encephalopathy; EEG has no role in a neuromuscular junction disorder (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

The signs are fatigable, AChR antibodies are positive and contrast MRI of brain and spine shows no leptomeningeal or cranial nerve enhancement; CSF cytology would not change management, and CSF has no role in MG.
FDG-PET belongs to the lymphoma response schedule; it does not answer the MG question, and contrast CT answers the thymic one.
Anthracycline echo surveillance belongs to the oncology schedule; it does not answer the MG question.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody-positive, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), paraneoplastic in context of peripheral T-cell lymphoma; concurrent vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy as a separate process

differential.diagnosis: Vincristine neurotoxicity alone (peripheral and cranial neuropathy)
differential.key_features: NCS show a length-dependent axonal sensory neuropathy that explains the distal signs and absent ankle reflexes; a vincristine cranial neuropathy would give fixed, not fatigable, ptosis and ophthalmoparesis without an ice-pack response. AChR antibodies and facial SFEMG show a coexisting MG.
VGCC antibodies negative, normal baseline CMAPs in the tested muscles and no post-exercise facilitation (11%), with prominent ocular signs and positive AChR antibodies.
EPOCH prednisone could cause proximal weakness, but not fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness.
Generalized fatigue does not produce focal fatigable cranial signs or abnormal jitter.

Contrast MRI of brain and spine shows no mass, leptomeningeal or cranial nerve enhancement, and the deficits fluctuate and fatigue; he is afebrile (37.1 C) and the MRI shows no lesion to suggest an opportunistic CNS infection.

key_clinical_evidence: Fatigable asymmetric ptosis, diplopia with fatigable left abduction weakness, nasal speech, jaw fatigue and fatigable proximal weakness are not explained by the length-dependent vincristine neuropathy.
Positive ice-pack test on the left (MRD1 +2.5 mm).
Anti-AChR binding 1.4 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies establishes AChR-positive MG; VGCC antibodies are negative.
RNS decrement is borderline (9% nasalis, 8% trapezius) without facilitation; SFEMG of orbicularis oculi shows increased jitter and blocking.
NCS confirm a separate length-dependent axonal sensory neuropathy consistent with vincristine toxicity.
Reduced FVC (70%, 40.8 mL/kg), MIP -48 and MEP 71 cmH2O with bulbar symptoms justify IVIG and monitored care.
Mediastinal CT shows no thymoma; thymectomy is deferred while stage IV lymphoma is on treatment and reconsidered in remission.
Recurrent febrile neutropenia makes MG-unsafe antibiotics (fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides) a practical risk.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Fatigable ptosis, diplopia and bulbar weakness with positive AChR antibodies and abnormal facial SFEMG indicate MG; the vincristine neuropathy is a separate, length-dependent process.
red_herrings.data_point: Active peripheral T-cell lymphoma on EPOCH chemotherapy with vincristine neuropathy and multiple febrile neutropenia episodes
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute weakness to chemotherapy fatigue, vincristine neuropathy or lymphoma progression.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild cytopenias are expected on EPOCH and do not explain fatigable ocular and bulbar weakness.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute weakness and fatigue to anemia; ignore MG.

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal or borderline RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal or borderline (Jacob 2025).

findings.description: Fatty involuted thymus. No anterior mediastinal mass or nodule.
Residual soft tissue, largest 1.3 cm short axis (right paratracheal), decreased from 3.1 cm on the prior staging CT.
No pulmonary mass, nodule or consolidation.

body_imaging.impression: CT chest with contrast: 1. No anterior mediastinal mass; fatty involuted thymus. 2. Residual right paratracheal and subcarinal nodal soft tissue (1.3 cm), decreased from the prior staging CT. 3. Lungs clear.

interactions: Vincristine: dose-dependent axonal neuropathy; no effect on neuromuscular junction transmission and no interaction with pyridostigmine.
Pyridostigmine increases gastrointestinal motility (diarrhea, cramps); it does not add to vincristine constipation.
Etoposide, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, filgrastim, ondansetron, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole: no interaction with pyridostigmine or IVIG and no recognized effect on neuromuscular transmission.
Prednisone is already part of EPOCH (days 1-5 of each cycle); additional corticosteroid adds to infection risk in a patient with recurrent neutropenia.
general.proposed: Pyridostigmine, IVIG, prednisone (screened against the current medication list and EPOCH)
warnings: Myasthenia gravis: avoid fluoroquinolones (including neutropenia prophylaxis) and aminoglycosides; choose an MG-safe beta-lactam for febrile neutropenia. Macrolides and IV magnesium also worsen MG.
IVIG: check renal function and hydrate; thrombotic risk is increased in active malignancy.

abnormal_values_summary: WBC 3.2 x10^9/L (L), hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL (L), platelets 142 x10^9/L (L)
labs.interpretation: Anti-AChR binding 1.4 nmol/L, blocking 24% and modulating 38%, all elevated; anti-MuSK and anti-VGCC P/Q-type not detected. Mild leukopenia (ANC 1800), anemia and thrombocytopenia. LDH elevated. Thyroid function, sodium, potassium and creatinine within reference ranges. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in a subset of patients with disorders of neuromuscular transmission; clinical correlation recommended.

results.finding: Pyridostigmine is the initial symptomatic treatment; IVIG or plasma exchange is used for severe or rapidly worsening weakness, including bulbar weakness; corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy are used when goals are not met.
results.source: Sanders DB et al. Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al. Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: Thymectomy improved clinical outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
results.source: Wolfe GI et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522

myasthenia gravis diagnosis and manageme.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122) recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fibre EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma. In the MGTX trial (Wolfe GI et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522) thymectomy improved outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.

Borderline decrement at 3 Hz in nasalis (9%) and trapezius (8%), below the 10% threshold; normal baseline CMAP amplitudes in the tested muscles and no post-exercise facilitation. 2. patient.chief_complaint: New bilateral ptosis and diplopia in a patient on chemotherapy for lymphoma

medications.drug: Dose-adjusted EPOCH (etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin)

past_medical_history: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (high-grade, stage IV), receiving dose-adjusted EPOCH chemotherapy, currently after cycle 4 of 6
Prior ICU admission for severe sepsis during chemotherapy cycle 2
Vincristine-associated peripheral neuropathy (distal sensory symptoms in the feet since cycle 2)

patient.history_present_illness: A 57-year-old man with high-grade peripheral T-cell lymphoma receiving EPOCH chemotherapy (after 4 of 6 planned cycles) presented with new bilateral ptosis and diplopia over 5 weeks. He had been doing well on chemotherapy with near-complete metabolic response on interim PET-CT, but his oncology team noted new drooping of his left eyelid at a clinic visit. The patient confirmed the ptosis had been present for 5 weeks and was progressive. He developed horizontal diplopia 3 weeks ago, initially intermittent and worse after a long day, and now present during most of his waking hours. He also reported jaw fatigue when eating and rested between bites during meals. His voice had become increasingly nasal, a change his wife noted clearly. He denied significant dysphagia. He had been attributing all new neurological symptoms to chemotherapy toxicity, which had already caused a vincristine peripheral neuropathy. He had multiple prior episodes of febrile neutropenia requiring hospitalization and had a severe sepsis episode after his second cycle requiring one week in the ICU. His oncologist was concerned about: (1) central nervous system lymphoma invasion, (2) paraneoplastic syndrome, (3) chemotherapy neurotoxicity (vincristine-induced cranial neuropathy), and (4) opportunistic infection. A contrast MRI of the brain and spine obtained by oncology last week was reported as showing no CNS lymphoma. He was referred to neurology for evaluation of the eye and bulbar symptoms.

neurological_exam.additional: No dysphagia currently. Mild jaw fatigue on eating. Speech becomes nasal after counting to 30.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral ptosis, left greater than right. MRD1 left 0.5 mm, right 2.5 mm. Fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze (left lid covers the pupil at 50 seconds). Horizontal diplopia on leftward gaze with limited left eye abduction that worsens with sustained gaze. Pupils equal, reactive. Bilateral facial weakness (orbicularis oculi and orbicularis oris). Voice nasal after sustained speech.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Mildly fatigued appearance. Normal language. Mildly slowed processing from chemotherapy-related fatigue.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal weakness: deltoids 4/5 bilaterally, hip flexors 4/5, both declining after repeated testing. Distal strength intact except mild toe extensor weakness bilaterally. No fasciculations.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 1+ in the arms and knees, ankle jerks absent (vincristine neuropathy). Plantar downgoing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild stocking-glove diminished sensation feet (vincristine peripheral neuropathy).

physical_exam.general: Weight 68.6 kg, height 172 cm. Thin, mildly fatigued, no respiratory distress. Alopecia.
